methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents intentional capability-building outside NoVA, but its success depends on whether evaluation translates to distributed implementation or remains aspirational—a critical inflection point between deepening regional capacity and reinforcing the metro-rural gap.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's BBB partnership to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses represents peer-to-peer knowledge distribution infrastructure that could enable broad, practical AI fluency across the small business ecosystem rather than platform-dependent shallow adoption.

signals.title: ODU, CHKD want to map hotspots of childhood asthma in Hampton Roads with AI - WHRO
signals.signal_reading: ODU-CHKD's AI-powered asthma mapping project demonstrates deep technical capability in Hampton Roads' healthcare-military corridor, but its institutional concentration raises questions about whether this expertise diffuses to community health workers or remains siloed in research institutions.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's executive order on AI cyber defense signals reactive policy posture focused on threat mitigation rather than proactive capability-building, potentially locking Virginia into vendor dependency without developing distributed internal expertise to implement sophisticated AI security.

signals.title: Rural advocacy groups band together to oppose data centers, related energy projects
signals.signal_reading: Rural coalitions opposing data centers reveal infrastructure extractivism anxiety—regions bearing energy/land costs of AI economy without capturing capability benefits, signaling neither depth nor distribution materializing in Virginia's most vulnerable communities.
